tr_keys.letCustomerScanQr: Let the customer scan this QR to pay online.
tr_keys.tillOfflineBanner: Till offline — payment confirms by code. The customer pays the link on their phone and reads you the 6-digit code from their payment screen; the sale syncs when you are back online.
tr_keys.enterSixDigitCode: Enter the 6-digit verification code shown on the customer's payment screen after successful payment.
tr_keys.invalidCode: That code doesn't match. Check it with the customer and try again.
tr_keys.printFailed: Printing failed — the sale was NOT recorded. Fix the printer or finish without a receipt.
tr_keys.creditRemainder: remains — the sale completes as a CREDIT order on the customer's account and auto-collects in full from their next wallet top-up (oldest debt first).
tr_keys.creditUnavailable: Credit unavailable — completing on credit would breach the shop's credit allowance.
tr_keys.deliveryNeedsAddress: Add a delivery address to send this order out.
tr_keys.deliveryNeedsCustomer: Attach a customer to send this order for delivery.
tr_keys.entersOrderQueue: enters the order queue · mark Ready when packed
tr_keys.quickFlowExplainer: Let the till run itself between customers — every switch here is per-shop
tr_keys.autoAcceptOrdersExplainer: New orders land as Accepted instead of waiting for a tap on the board
tr_keys.autoAcceptPlatformGate: Also needs the platform switch Auto Approve All Orders — with both on, checkout writes the order straight to Accepted
tr_keys.autoCompleteAtReadyExplainer: The moment an order is marked Ready it completes itself
tr_keys.autoCompleteAtReadyWarning: Orders complete without anyone handing them over — nobody taps to confirm the customer took it, so only turn this on where the customer is already standing at the counter, and only pickup orders are completed
tr_keys.keypadAutodialExplainer: With nothing on the ticket, a digit key adds its preset item — cash-register style
tr_keys.quickFlowAllThreeOn: A shop with all three on
tr_keys.quickFlowStep1Body: The customer pays, and a digit key puts the item on the ticket — no menu hunting
tr_keys.quickFlowStep2Body: It is born Accepted — never sits in the New column waiting for a tap
tr_keys.quickFlowStep3Body: Ready completes itself — staff serve the customer while the board clears behind them
tr_keys.autodialArmedHint: Autodial is on — tap a digit to drop its preset straight on the ticket, and once an item is on the keys are money again
tr_keys.keysAreMoneyAgain: Ticket has an item — the keys are money again

integrations._comment: Pairs with auth_sdk >= 1.9.0's @auth-entry-config placeholder (Users repo). Ray's rule: Skip (guest entry) lives in the shared login page and shows in ALL apps by default; a home SDK that doesn't need it opts out — 'delivery and merchants dont need it'. On older auth_sdk the marker is absent and the installer only warns (wiring NOT applied), leaving behavior unchanged.

boot_hooks._comment: Registers this SDK's bundled Afrikaans map for its manifest tr_keys into base_sdk's BundledTranslations registry at boot. Backend-served translation rows still win; the map is only the offline/unseeded fallback consulted before the humanized-key fallback. Requires a base_sdk with bundled_translations.dart.

Path and route name match paas_manager's existing hand-written CupertinoRoute(path: '/list-notification', page: NotificationListRoute.page), so the composed restaurant tab's context.pushRoute(const NotificationListRoute()) keeps working when the host deletes its own copy of the page and drops the hand-written route.

boot_hooks._comment: Windows notification delivery, POS parity (1.6.0): firebase_messaging has no Windows implementation, so the FCM hook above deliberately excludes Windows and composed Windows exes shipped with NO notification path at all. This hook starts comms' DesktopNotificationPoller (10s REST count polling + looping POS notification.wav + ValueNotifier badge feed - see the service's doc comment) on Windows only. The start is deferred to addPostFrameCallback because boot-hook bodies run BEFORE LocalStorage.init() and the sdk-di block in the generated main.dart: by first frame both are done, and runApp is never delayed by a poll. Fail-open try/catch like the FCM hook - a boot failure debugPrints instead of blanking the app. WidgetsBinding resolves via main.dart's static material import; foundation dedupes with the FCM hook's wiring import. Toast layer (still 1.6.0, same unmerged PR): poller.start() also initializes LocalNotifications fail-open (flutter_local_notifications 19.x WindowsInitializationSettings - stable hardcoded GUID, APP_NAME/WINDOWS_AUMID dart-defines for branding, works unpackaged; MSIX identity optional host-side) and each count increase raises a native toast via LocalNotifications.show() alongside the sound - no hook body change needed, the toast path lives entirely inside the service.

embedded_widgets._comment: Header slot (ADR-005): shells embed the compact adaptive widget without importing weather_sdk directly. inlineExpansion=false because headers are height-constrained; on small screens that leaves just the minimal icon+temp chip, and the popup-free WeatherInlineForecast card is placed in body flow via the weather_sdk barrel (it takes a WeatherState argument, so it cannot ride the zero-arg embedded-widget seam).

Severe-weather heads-up banner (zero-arg seam, ADR-005): hosts place it in body flow; it renders SizedBox.shrink() whenever there are no active warnings, the warnings cmd fails, or the composed backend does not expose tenant.api.get_weather_warnings yet - so embedding it is always safe, in any merge order with the backend rollout. Location comes from the same WeatherSdkConfig.locationResolver the header widget's install template wires.

boot_hooks._comment: Registers this SDK's bundled Afrikaans map for its manifest tr_keys into base_sdk's BundledTranslations registry at boot. Top-level (not app_type-gated) because translations are role-agnostic. Backend-served translation rows still win; the map is only the offline/unseeded fallback consulted before the humanized-key fallback. Requires a base_sdk with bundled_translations.dart.

Backend-served translation rows still win; the map is only the offline/unseeded fallback consulted before the humanized-key fallback. Top-level (not app_type-gated) because translations are role-agnostic.

Order 30: after comms' Firebase/FCM boot (10) and its desktop notification poller (20) - order 20 is already taken and duplicate orders draw a composer warning. Android-only and fail-open like comms' hooks. The initialize() call itself is a strict no-op unless DeviceServices proves the device GMS-free AND HMS-capable, so GMS devices and detection errors keep comms_sdk's FCM path as the sole push owner. The await is cheap: initialize() only awaits the availability probe and turnOnPush - the push token arrives asynchronously on Push Kit's token stream, so runApp is never delayed by a token round-trip.

di_hooks._comment: The visibility flag without a core change: wraps the registered SettingsRepositoryFacade (comms_sdk) so getGlobalSettings() carries `reservation_enable_for_user` from the booking-owned `api.booking.get_booking_settings` (Permission Settings enable_reservations). base_sdk's AppHelpers.getReservationEnable() and marketplace's profile gate then work unchanged. Order 30 so it runs after every *SdkDependencies.register (the installer emits di_hooks after the generated DI block) and after sibling hooks that might register the facade. Fail-open: a booking failure leaves the inner result untouched.

Registers SellerBookingRepositoryFacade (demo-gated) and the RESERVATIONS group (ProfileSection id booking.reservations, order 135) on base_sdk's ProfileSectionRegistry, which is how the manager profile host reaches the three routes above without merchants_sdk changing. Order 14: after orders' manager DI (10), before its POS facades (20); it depends on neither.
